properties.areaDesc: Pinal, AZ
properties.headline: Dust Storm Warning issued October 16 at 8:40AM MST until October 16 at 10:45AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Dust Storm Warning for...
Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1045 AM MST.

* At 840 AM MST, a plume of dust was located 9 miles north of
Maricopa, or 8 miles west of Sun Lakes, and was stationary along
Highway 347.

HAZARD...Less than a quarter mile visibility with strong wind gusts
in excess of 40 mph.

SOURCE...Satellite and highway camera observations.

IMPACT...Dangerous life-threatening travel.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Pinal County.

This includes AZ Route 347 between mile markers 180 and 184.
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not drive into a dust storm. PULL ASIDE STAY ALIVE!

Dust storms lead to dangerous driving conditions with visibility
reduced to near zero. If driving, avoid dust storms if possible. If
caught in one, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep your
foot off the brake.

There is no safe place on a highway when a dust storm hits.
Visibility can be lost immediately, making it difficult or impossible
to slow down and avoid stopped vehicles. Delay travel, or safely exit
the highway before the dust storm arrives.

CMAMtext: NWS: DUST STORM WARNING til 10:45 AM MST. Be ready for a sudden drop to zero visibility.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: DUST STORM WARNING for this area until 10:45 AM MST. Be ready for sudden drop to zero visibility. Pull Aside, Stay Alive! When visibility drops, pull far off the road and put your vehicle in park. Turn the lights off and keep your foot off the brake. Infants, the elderly and those with respiratory issues urged to take precautions.

properties.areaDesc: Tucson Metro Area including Tucson/Green Valley/Marana/Vail
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 16 at 8:36AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
The Pima County Department of Environmental Quality (PDEQ) has
issued a Dust Action Day for the Tucson Metro area until 8 PM MST
this evening.

An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate
widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-
10 concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air
pollutant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in outdoor physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

For details on this Action Day, visit the PDEQ website at
www.pima.gov/deq or call 520-724-6885.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 10:44AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Saturday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. Strong northeasterly winds this weekend will slow
or even reverse flow, causing the river to rise back into Moderate
Flood Stage, with a steady increase through Moderate Flood Stage
forecast through early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane. At
3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near
Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Friday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Friday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early next
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 16 at 4:49AM AKDT until October 17 at 1:30AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Nuisance flooding on roadways and small stream flooding
caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Roadways within the Mendenhall Valley, areas around Montana
Creek and Jordan Creek.

* WHEN...Until 130 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding on roadways impacting the Friday morning commute. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 441 AM AKDT, satellite estimates indicate heavy rain ongoing
across the advisory area. Rapid river rises will cause nusiance
flooding of roadways, poor drainage areas, and small streams
reaching bankfull conditions, especially near Montana Creek And
Jordan Creek. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain has fallen in
the last 12 hours. The heaviest rainfall rates of 0.2 to 0.3
inches in 1 hour are expected through the next couple of hours
before quickly diminishing into Friday morning. Additional
rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible.
- For Jordan Creek near Juneau:
At 4:00am the stage was 8.3 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.7 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 9.2 feet is expected around 9:00am
Friday.

Impacts:
At 9.2 feet: This is the stage when Jordan Creek is at bankfull and
water will begin to inundate areas along the edges of the creek near
Race Reality and Jordan Square.
At 9.7 feet: Water will inundate the Jordan Square's front and back
parking lots, around Jordan Creek office condominiums with up to one
foot of water. Some residential driveways will be flooded and cut
off.

For Montana Creek at Back Loop Bridge:
At 12:00pm the stage was 11.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 14.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 14.5 feet is expected around 7:00am
Friday.

Impacts:
At 14.5 feet: Water begins flowing over the low water crossing on
Montana Creek Road. Bankfull conditions at the gauge with water
starting to inundate adjacent undeveloped fields along Mendenhall
Loop Road.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued October 16 at 10:48PM ChST until October 19 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large, hazardous breaking
waves of 7 to 9 feet Saturday afternoon will become dangerous,
building to as high as 35 feet for Guam, 25 feet for Rota and 20
feet for Tinian and Saipan. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...For the High Surf Warning, initially east facing reefs
of Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan; spreading to all reefs
through Sunday afternoon. The Coastal Flood Watch is also for
all reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 5 PM Saturday to 4 AM
ChST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Saturday
afternoon through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous
seas. Life-threatening swimming conditions and significant
beach erosion can be expected. Coastal inundation of 5 to 7 feet
for Guam, 2 to 4 feet for Rota and 1 to 3 feet for Tinian and
Saipan is possible along with coastal flooding and beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As TS Champi approaches the Marianas, surf
conditions are expected to deteriorate rapidly, with surf
reaching 9 feet Saturday afternoon, building to dangerous/deadly
levels through Saturday night.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued October 16 at 10:48PM ChST until October 19 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large, hazardous breaking
waves of 7 to 9 feet Saturday afternoon will become dangerous,
building to as high as 35 feet for Guam, 25 feet for Rota and 20
feet for Tinian and Saipan. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...For the High Surf Warning, initially east facing reefs
of Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan; spreading to all reefs
through Sunday afternoon. The Coastal Flood Watch is also for
all reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 5 PM Saturday to 4 AM
ChST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Saturday
afternoon through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous
seas. Life-threatening swimming conditions and significant
beach erosion can be expected. Coastal inundation of 5 to 7 feet
for Guam, 2 to 4 feet for Rota and 1 to 3 feet for Tinian and
Saipan is possible along with coastal flooding and beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As TS Champi approaches the Marianas, surf
conditions are expected to deteriorate rapidly, with surf
reaching 9 feet Saturday afternoon, building to dangerous/deadly
levels through Saturday night.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 16 at 7:45AM CDT until October 17 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph expected.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southwest Alabama, northwest
Florida, and southeast Mississippi.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 7 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong and gusty winds will be capable of downing
numerous additional compromised trees which would result in renewed
power outages in vulnerable areas impacted by the extreme winds
during Hurricane Isaias. In addition, large debris piles from storm
cleanup may be blown about resulting in additional hazards to
anyone nearby outdoors along with potentially blocking previously
cleared roadways. Additional road closures will be possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Many trees are leaning over power lines,
homes, and roads in the impacted area. Frequent wind gusts forecast
between 35 and 40 mph will create dangerous conditions outdoors in
the vulnerable areas. Elsewhere, winds may result in large tree
branches downed and localized power outages.
properties.instruction:
Use extreme caution if you must travel or be outdoors Friday night
through Saturday. Remain alert for potential falling trees and power
lines, blown debris, and additional damage to structures that remain
compromised from the hurricane.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 16 at 4:41AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
An atmospheric river system will continue to bring multiple rounds
of moderate to heavy rainfall to the area, with an additional 1.0 to
1.5 inches through Friday morning. Localized higher amounts are
possible due to terrain effects. Overall the moderate to heavy
rainfall is expected to persist through the morning hours before
starting to diminish later this morning.

Montana Creek and Jordan Creek are expected to reach bankfull
Friday morning, after these rounds of heavy rainfall. Other
creeks and rivers in the Juneau area will still see rises through
this morning, however no flooding is anticipated for other streams
at this time.

properties.areaDesc: Guam
properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 16 at 9:43PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TROPICAL STORM CHAMPI INTENSIFYING AND MOVING WEST TOWARDS THE
MARIANAS...
...CHAMPI LIKELY TO MOVE NEAR GUAM AS A TYPHOON...

.NEW INFORMATION...
Guam was placed in Condition of Readiness 2 as of 1 PM ChST.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions for
people on Guam and on Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the Northern
Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.

A Tropical storm warning and a Typhoon Watch continue for Tinian
and Saipan.

A Flood Watch is in effect for all of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might
be in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 8 PM ChST...the center of Tropical Storm Champi (29W) was located
near latitude 11.6N...longitude 152.1E. This was about 510 miles
east-southeast of Guam. Storm motion was west, 275 degrees, at 13 mph.
Storm intensity was 60 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
TS Champi continues to head toward Guam. Along the way, Rota will be
affected by lesser but still damaging winds toward the outside of
Champi. Tinian and Saipan will be just grazed by the edge.

.PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
properties.instruction:
Make the final preparations to protect life and property. Rush
to completion the hardening of your home or business by closing
shutters and bracing garage doors.

If evacuating, leave as soon as possible. Guard against being
stuck out on roadways when dangerous winds and heavy rains
arrive. Again, do not stay in a metal roof or container home.
Remember, pets are not allowed in most official shelters, so
check ahead with your intended shelter.

If staying in a home, turn the refrigerator to maximum cold and
keep it closed. Turn off propane tanks and unplug small
appliances. Fill the bathtub with water in case the tap water
becomes unavailable after the storm. This is for cleaning and
flushing purposes. Do not drink it.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 16 at 6:41AM CDT until October 17 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
* WIND...North winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph behind
a cold front.

* HUMIDITY...Minimum Relative Humidity values between 25 to 40
percent.

* FUELS...Critically dry.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures will
create favorable weather for rapid fire growth and spread. Avoid
activities that promote open flames and sparks.

A Fire Weather Watch means that the potential for critical fire
weather conditions exists. These conditions could promote the
rapid spread of wildfires which could become life-threatening.
Check www.weather.gov/jan/fireweather for forecast updates and a
possible upgrade of this watch to a Red Flag Warning.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 16 at 3:26AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A series of fronts is bringing multiple rounds of moderate to heavy
rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle as of early Friday morning.
This second round of heavy rain has brought around 2 to 3 inches of
rainfall to the area over the last 24 hours, with ongoing moderate
rainfall rates of around 0.1 to 0.2 inches reported within the last
hour. An additional 0.5 to 1 inch of rain is expected into late
Friday morning as this system pushes out of the area. Highest rain
amounts are expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands, with locally
lower or higher amounts possible due to terrain effects. Heaviest
rainfall rates will come to an end through Friday morning with
intermittent rain showers continuing through Friday afternoon across
the area.

While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to
small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding
anticipated at this time.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
situation and update our forecast.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 16 at 6:11AM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 7 AM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

receive information from authorities.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 2:47AM CDT until October 18 at 6:44AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP, Texas
affecting Brewster County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande above Rio Conchos near
Presidio,  Texas, Test Forecast Point A, Rio Grande at Presidio
Vehicle Bridge, Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near Presidio,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near
Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Dryden,  Texas, Terlingua Creek near Terlingua,
Texas...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP,
Texas.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, and no damage
is expected.  Preparations may be necessary to remove water pumps.
The park should be notified at this time if additional rises are
expected so they will have time to remove the pumps. At 13.0 feet,
the river reaches minor flood stage.  Water reaches the water pumps
maintained by the park service that are used to water the
campgrounds and to provide water to the employee living quarters.
It may be necessary for park personnel to remove the pumps. At 15.0
feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage.  Water pumps
submerge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 AM CDT Friday the stage was 1.4 feet (0.4 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage early this
morning to 16.7 feet (5.1 meters) late this morning. It will then
fall below flood stage this evening to 5.7 feet (1.7 meters) late
tomorrow morning. It will rise to 6.3 feet (1.9 meters) tomorrow
afternoon. It will then fall again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet (4.0 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.5
feet (5.0 meters) on 05/28/2023.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 300 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 16 at 12:17AM PDT until October 16 at 11:00AM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 AM PDT THIS MORNING
DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTH BAY INTERIOR
MOUNTAINS...

* AFFECTED AREA...North Bay Interior Mountains.

* TIMING...Until 11 AM PDT this morning.

* WINDS 20 FOOT...North winds 10 to 15 mph with gusts between 30 to
40 mph. The highest peaks above 4000 ft will see gusts up to 60
mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 13 to 23 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning is issued when weather conditions that promote
rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening are forecast.
This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either
occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple
ways to receive information from authorities.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them
completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a
spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks.
Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember,
one less spark, one less flame.

Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan! Where will you go? How
will you get there? Do you have your go kit ready to go? Who will you
call to let others know you are safe? Visit ready.gov/plan for more
information.

NWSheadline: RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 AM PDT THIS MORNING

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 16 at 2:07AM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 3 to 13 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 7 AM CDT this
morning through Sunday morning. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, from 1 PM this afternoon to 7 AM CDT Sunday. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM this afternoon to 7 AM CDT
Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian Coastal Waters; Saipan Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Typhoon Watch issued October 16 at 4:51PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Tropical storm conditions, including winds of 34 to 63
knots, are expected. Typhoon conditions, including winds of 64
knots or more are possible within the next 48 hours.

* WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Onset of damaging winds beginning Saturday night,
continuing into at least Sunday night, possibly longer if
conditions warrant.

* IMPACTS...Destructive winds will produce dangerous seas that
could damage, capsize or sink vessels, along with drastically
reducing visibilities in heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tropical Storm Champi (29W) continues to
move quickly toward the Marianas. The exact path of 29W remains
subject to change. However, guidance supports a passage through
Guam coastal waters, with damaging winds moving into Tinian and
Saipan Saturday night and lasting into at least Sunday night.
Champi is expected to strengthen further today and Saturday as
it approaches, then move through the region as a typhoon Sunday
morning. Seas will quickly rise, with significant sea heights
reaching as high as 25 feet during closest passage of Champi.
Dangerous sea conditions may continue into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for tropical storm
force conditions Sunday morning. Secure all vessels. Conditions
are expected to be catastrophic for small craft, and extremely
dangerous for any vessels of larger size. As Tropical Storm Champi
approaches the Marianas, stay in safe harbor.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 16 at 12:21AM CDT until October 17 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE SATURDAY...

.A cold front will move through the area later today bringing very
dry air with RH values falling into the low to mid 30s along with
windy conditions with some gusts around 30 mph. The combination of
gusty winds, current drought conditions, ample dry fuel, and very
dry conditions will allow any fire that develops to spread
quickly.

* AFFECTED AREA...Pearl River, Hancock, Harrison and Jackson.

* WINDS...North 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 32 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph expected.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Alabama and Big Bend and Panhandle
Florida.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 7 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and
compromised trees. Trees damaged from Hurricane Isaias will be
extra vulnerable to the elevated winds that may result in more
downed trees in the area. In addition, large debris piles from
storm cleanup may be blown about resulting in additional hazards to
anyone nearby outdoors. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Frequent wind gusts forecast around 30-35 mph
will create dangerous conditions outdoors in the vulnerable areas.
Elsewhere, winds may result in large tree branches downed and
localized power outages.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

Remain alert for potential falling trees and power lines, blown
debris, and additional damage to structures that remain compromised
from the hurricane.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 15 at 11:58PM CDT until October 17 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL
AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY...

.Breezy and dry conditions due to a frontal passage will combine
with very dry fuels and produce red flag conditions across
portions of central and southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas
through Friday afternoon. A Fire Weather Watch is in place for
all of southeast Texas and southwest and central Louisiana on
Saturday.

...FIRE WEATHER WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM SATURDAY MORNING
THROUGH SATURDAY EVENING FOR HIGH WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY
FOR PORTIONS OF CENTRAL AND SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA AND SOUTHEAST
TEXAS...

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 027 Vernon, Fire Weather
Zone 028 Rapides, Fire Weather Zone 029 Avoyelles, Fire
Weather Zone 030 Beauregard, Fire Weather Zone 180 Tyler, Fire
Weather Zone 259 Northern Jasper and Fire Weather Zone 260
Northern Newton.

* TIMING...For the Red Flag Warning, from 11 AM Friday to 1 AM
CDT Saturday. For the Fire Weather Watch, from Saturday
morning through Saturday evening.

* WINDS...North 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 82 Friday, Up to 72 Saturday.

* LIGHTNING...

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 16 at 2:31PM ChST until October 18 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota, Saipan and Tinian.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street
flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Tropical Storm Champi is approaching the Marianas and will bring
torrential rain Saturday night and Sunday at least. Total
rainfall accumulations of 12 to 20 inches are possible for Guam,
10 to 18 inches for Rota and 8 to 12 inches for Tinian and
Saipan. This could cause flooding problems in poor drainage and
flood prone areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SUNDAY AFTERNOON

Thursday evening, lasting through Friday morning. Multiple waves

possible.

expected through this evening, where rates could exceed 0.5
inches per hour.

mph at sea level, and exceeding 60 mph at elevation, with the

possibility for isolated landslides along steep mountain slopes.

properties.areaDesc: Lake Casitas; Ojai Valley
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 15 at 1:16PM PDT until October 17 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
...HIGH RISK FOR RAPID FIRE GROWTH AND EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH
ANY NEW FIRE STARTS THROUGH SATURDAY, DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY
STRONG SANTA ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

.Updates include adding the following areas to the previous Red
Flag Warnings - Ojai, Casitas, and the Santa Lucia Mountains.
Moderate to strong Santa Ana winds will peak around Friday then
slowly weaken through the weekend. Meanwhile, dry air will persist
and dry out any effects of the recent rains. Red Flag Warnings
are in effect for most of Los Angeles and Ventura Counties
Thursday through Saturday, and for interior Santa Barbara and San
Luis Obispo Counties for Friday.

The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a
Red Flag Warning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in
effect until 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Lake Casitas and Ojai Valley.

* TIMING...Until 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...East 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 40 mph, strongest Friday.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 8 to 15 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 15 at 9:47AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
AQATWC

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued a
PM-10 High Pollution Advisory for Douglas on Friday.

An episode of strong and gusty winds is forecast to generate
widespread blowing dust that may result in local PM-10 concentrations
that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects increase as air
quality deteriorates.

Coarse particulate matter - also known as PM-10 - is an air
contaminant that can aggravate heart and lung disease conditions,
especially in older adults, children, and those with asthma. A
decrease in physical activity is recommended.

Consolidate your travel, stabilize loose soils, slow down or avoid
travel on dirt roads, reduce or eliminate fireplace use, and avoid
using gas-powered lawn equipment.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory,
visit the ADEQ internet site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/douglas or
call 602-771-2300.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Guam, GU; Rota, MP; Saipan, MP; Tinian, MP
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 13 at 5:31PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend.

This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible.

As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later this weekend.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.

NWSheadline: INCREASING POTENTIAL FOR HEAVY RAINFALL AND FLOODING THIS WEEKEND FOR THE MARIANAS
